title: Canary Burn Sprint: Traffic Fence & KPI Matrix
body:
Summary
This is a working doc for the short, instrumented canary we want to run ahead of a broader feature rollout (target: mid-March). Focus: define traffic fencing, minimum sample sizes, KPI burn targets, operator runbook steps, and the decision thresholds that auto-trigger rollback or scale-up.

Context and goals
- Feature: adaptive batching + new caching layer for hosted inference. Expected benefits: 20–30% per-token CPU/GPU cost reduction in steady state, slight increase in tail latency for cold KV cache misses.
- Rollout strategy: 3-step canary (internal -> beta customers -> gradual public ramp). This doc covers step 2 -> the gated external canary that needs product-ops and SRE on-call.
- Success criteria: measurable cost reduction without violating latency SLOs beyond a short, explained transient.

Key constraints (notes to self)
- We must not exceed token-cost-burn budget for the canary window: $12k/week allocated.
- Security/PII: beta traffic is already consented; confirm with Privacy if cache logs contain any PII (TODO: Ellen).
- Observability hooks: token-level breakdown, per-model latency p95/p99, KV cache hit-rate, batch size distribution. If any of these metrics are missing, abort and roll back to previous model-only path.

KPI matrix (operational thresholds)
- Table (CSV-style):
metric,baseline,canary-target,soft-trigger,hard-trigger,owner
avg-latency-95(ms),120,<=140,>180 for 15m,>250 for 5m,SRE-Oncall
error-rate(% requests),0.3,<=0.6,>1.0 for 10m,>2.0 for 5m,Product-Ops
kv-cache-hit-rate(%),12,>=30,drop >=10pp over 30m,drop >=20pp over 10m,Applied-ML
token-cost-per-1k,0.95,<=0.75,>1.2 for 1h,>1.5 for 30m,Finance-Observer
throughput-reqs/s,250,>=230,drop 30% sustained 20m,drop 50% sustained 10m,Serving-Runtime

Interpretation: soft-trigger means alert to humans and start mitigating steps (reduce traffic, increase sampling), hard-trigger means immediate rollback.

Canary choreography (timeline)
- Day -3: final smoke in staging with production snapshot of traffic (traffic-shadowed minimal load). Confirm dashboards green.
- Day -1: Dry run with 1% internal traffic (engineering + product). Collect baseline.
- Day 0: Open beta gate to 2% external traffic for 6 hours. Monitor closely.
- Day 0+1: If green, move to 10% for 12 hours. If green, 25% for 24 hours, then gradual ramp by 10% increments every 12–24 hours with gating.
- Stop conditions: hard-trigger fires, dashboard missing key metrics, budget exceeded.

Sampling & statistical notes
- Minimum sample per interval for p95 estimation: 10k requests per 1-hour window. If traffic below that, extend the interval to 3 hours before making decisions.
- For cost estimates, compare token-cost burn vs. baseline with bootstrapped 95% CI. If CI overlaps zero saving, consider more data before rollout.

Operator runbook (quick actions)
- On soft-trigger:
  1) Notify #prod-rollouts and #sre-oncall with snapshot link.
  2) Reduce external canary traffic by 50% via traffic-fence toggle.
  3) Enable debug-level cache logging for next 30 minutes.
  4) Open triage call if metric doesn't recover in 20 minutes.
- On hard-trigger:
  1) Execute immediate rollback to previous deployment (runbook script: rollback-canary.sh).
  2) Pause all canary traffic and set traffic-fence to 0%.
  3) Notify exec on-call and product leadership + create incident in Jira (tag: INCIDENT-ROLLBACK).
  4) Collect artifacts: logs, traces, kv-cache snapshots, and attach to incident.

Observability checklist (must-have before opening beta)
- Model-level tracing instrumented (yes)
- Token-cost meter enabled per route (yes)
- KV cache hit-rate visible with 1m granularity (must be enabled)
- Alerts configured for soft/hard thresholds in the KPI matrix (SRE)
- Canary dashboard link: https://observability.redwood.com/dashboards/canary/CB-2025-03

Rollback decision rubric (human in loop)
- If hard-trigger fires: auto rollback. No debate.
- If soft-trigger fires: convene triage within 10 minutes. If root cause is transient (downstream DB, region flakiness), consider retrying with reduced traffic after 30–60 minutes. If cause is new feature regressions (error patterns, drastic tail latency), rollback.

Communication plan
- Pre-launch (24h): notify beta customers via support thread (Sofia owns). Provide expected impacts and contact path.
- During canary: hourly summary posted to #beta-rollouts. Real-time updates to stakeholders via the incident channel if triggers fire.
- Post-canary: 1 pager with KPI delta (Ravi to draft) and retro within 3 business days.

Open questions / TODOs
- Ellen: confirm PII safe on cache logs and update privacy signoff. (Due: 2025-02-14)
- Finance: clarify if token-cost budget can be extended if early savings are observed. (Daniel)
- Applied-ML: add a small synthetic test that simulates cold-cache miss patterns to ensure we capture worst-case tail latency. (Ravi)
- Product-Ops: create a short-run test harness that can replay a 10k request window locally for offline verification. (Maya)

Mini-scenarios (what to expect and scripts to run)
- Scenario A: Cold cache storm. Expected: p99 jump for 2–5 minutes, p95 within soft-trigger. Mitigation: throttle traffic by 30%, enable cache-warming for top-10 prefixes.
- Scenario B: Unexpected error spike tied to batching logic. Expected: error-rate jump. Mitigation: toggle batching to conservative mode (flag: batching-mode=small-batches) then evaluate.
- Scenario C: Unexpected cost spike from tokenization change. Expected: token-cost rewrite. Mitigation: block feature and start cost forensics.

Appendix: quick-check checklist (one page)
- [ ] Privacy signoff on cache logs
- [ ] Dashboards + alerts validated in staging
- [ ] Canary rollback script smoke-tested
- [ ] Support thread template ready
- [ ] Finance budget set and watcher on-duty

Notes to reviewers
This is intentionally operational and prescriptive; please comment inline for missing owners or thresholds that seem too conservative/aggressive. I expect a lot of iteration; the goal is to have a repeatable, low-friction checklist for future canaries of similar complexity.

Document history
- 2025-02-12: initial draft (Maya)
- 2025-02-18: added KPI matrix and operator runbook after SRE sync (Daniel)
- 2025-03-01: tightened thresholds and added sample-size guidance (Ravi)
